grants.title: APPRENTICESHIP EXPANSION GRANT (AEG-4) Request for Applications (RFA)
grants.summary: Funds the expansion of New York State Registered Apprenticeship training to increase employment opportunities for approximately 130 apprentices, focusing on underrepresented populations.
grants.description: The New York State Department of Labor (NYSDOL) is offering up to $3M in funding under the Apprenticeship Expansion Grant (AEG-4) to expand Registered Apprenticeship (RA) training in New York State. The grant aims to increase employment opportunities for approximately 130 apprentices, particularly from underrepresented populations, in high-demand occupations such as Advanced Manufacturing, Healthcare, Hospitality, and Information Technology. Construction trades are excluded unless related to facility upkeep and maintenance. Applicants can submit questions via email until August 16, 2024, and answers will be posted on the NYSDOL website. Applications are due by August 5, 2024.
grants.award_text: Up to $300,000 in single award amounts
grants.eligibility_notes: Eligible applicants include Not-For-Profit, For Profit, Governmental Entity, Tribal Organization, and Individual entities.
sdg_alignment: SDG 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth
key_requirements: Applicants must focus on expanding Registered Apprenticeships in New York State.
Apprenticeships must target high-demand occupations such as Advanced Manufacturing, Healthcare, Hospitality, and Information Technology.
Construction trades are excluded unless related to facility upkeep and maintenance.
Applicants must submit questions via email by August 16, 2024.
Applications must be submitted by August 5, 2024.

Solicitation Profile
The New York State Department of Labor (NYSDOL) is making up to $3M in Title I Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) Statewide Activities funding available under the Apprenticeship Expansion Grant (AEG-4) Request for Applications (RFA).  The purpose of this RFA is to expand New York State (NYS) Registered Apprenticeship (RA) training by increasing employment opportunities for approximately 130 apprentices, with a focus on underrepresented populations.  These apprentices will enter trades in high-demand occupations, with a focus on the emerging fields of Advanced Manufacturing, Healthcare, Hospitality, and Information Technology, as well as other in-demand occupations.  Please note that this solicitation focuses on promoting the expansion of NYS RAs and as such, RAs in the field of Construction are not eligible for funding under this RFA unless the trade is to be used for the upkeep and maintenance of a facility owned by the business entity employing the apprentice, such as plant maintenance trades.

grants.title: Direct Entry Pre-Apprenticeship (DEPA) Programs Request for Applications (RFA)
grants.summary: Funds programs to support approximately 300 participants and facilitate entry into NYS Registered Apprenticeship programs for underrepresented populations.
grants.description: The New York State Department of Labor (NYSDOL) is offering up to $2 million in funding for Direct Entry Pre-Apprenticeship Programs (DEPA). These programs aim to provide training and exposure to various trades, supporting entry into NYS Registered Apprenticeship programs for underrepresented groups such as women, minorities, individuals with disabilities, and veterans. Targeted industries include Building and Construction, Manufacturing, and Information Technology. Applications are accepted through Grants Gateway until March 29, 2024, and organizations must meet prequalification requirements.
grants.eligibility_notes: Eligible applicants include For Profit, Governmental Entity, and Not-For-Profit organizations.
sdg_alignment: SDG 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth
key_requirements: Applicants must be prequalified in the Statewide Financial System (SFS) after January 16, 2024.
Programs must support entry into NYS Registered Apprenticeship programs.
Focus on underrepresented populations including women, minorities, individuals with disabilities, and veterans.

Solicitation Profile
The New York State Department of Labor (NYSDOL) is making up to $2 million in State Apprenticeship Expansion Formula (SAEF) funding available under the Direct Entry Pre-Apprenticeship Programs (DEPA) Request for Applications (RFA).  The purpose of the RFA is to:
1. Provide funding for DEPA programs to support approximately 300 participants; and
2. Support entry into NYS Registered Apprenticeship (RA) programs for underrepresented
populations including women, minorities, individuals with disabilities, and veterans.
NYSDOL is particularly interested in supporting DEPA programs that provide participants with training and exposure to various trades and offer opportunities for entry into RA training programs. Targeted industries include, but are not limited to, Building and Construction, Manufacturing, and Information Technology (IT).
Although grantmaking activities will transition from the Grants Gateway to the Statewide Financial System (SFS) on January 16, 2024, applications for this funding opportunity will continue to be accepted through Grants Gateway until the submission deadline date of March 29, 2024.
Note: With the transition of grantmaking activities from the Grants Gateway to SFS, prequalification will be unavailable from December 15, 2023 through January 16, 2024.  After January 16, 2024, organizations will prequalify in SFS.  If an organization is prequalified at the time of the cutover, their prequalification status will move over to SFS.  Additional information regarding prequalification can be found at https://grantsmanagement.ny.gov/transition-SFS.

grants.title: Drinking Water Fluoridation – Rolling Submissions - Component A: Planning and Feasibility Projects

grants.description: The New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH) provides funding to eligible municipalities to develop Engineering Reports for feasibility studies or upgrades to community water fluoridation systems. The grant aims to increase access to fluoridated water for NYS residents. Applicants must document proposed municipal drinking water fluoridation projects using provided documents. Applications are submitted through the Grants Gateway portal.

grants.eligibility_notes: Eligible applicants are New York State municipalities.
key_requirements: Applicant must be a New York State municipality.
Must propose a municipal drinking water fluoridation project.
Must utilize provided documents for feasibility studies or system upgrades.

The New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH), Division of Family Health (DFH), Bureau of Child Health (BCH) announces the availability of funding through this Request for Applications (RFA) to maintain and expand New York State (NYS) residents’ access to optimally fluoridated water. The purpose of this RFA is to identify eligible NYS municipalities that want to work with NYS to increase the number of communities with access to fluoridated water. The key characteristic of a successful applicant is the ability to document a proposed NYS municipal drinking water fluoridation project utilizing the documents provided.  Component A is for eligible municipalities seeking to develop an Engineering Report to determine the feasibility of starting community water fluoridation or upgrade/modify an existing fluoridation system.
The total funding available is $2.5 million annually. As stated in the Term of Contract (Section G), 24-month term, with a start date approximately six months from award letter date. Component A applicants may request up to $50,000 for the full contract term. Total funding for Component A is projected to be $500,000 annually.
PLEASE NOTE: Letter of Interest is not required. Questions are accepted continuously until September 25, 2028 and answers will be posted as received and until September 27, 2028. Please see RFA for further info. To apply for this opportunity please go to the top of this page and login to the Grants Gateway. Search for “Available Opportunities” and look for the grant opportunity name listed above.
